newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada confirms losing WTO verdict on magazines.
newsitem.headline: Canada confirms losing WTO verdict on magazines.

text.p: A Canadian government official confirmed on Monday that Canada has lost a World Trade Organization ruling on its protectionist policies against foreign magazines.
The WTO dispute panel issued an interim ruling against Canada in January and last Friday it handed down a final decision to the two disputing parties -- the United States and Canada.

"The actual decision didn't change one iota," said Janet Bax, spokeswoman for Canadian Heritage Minister Sheila Copps, who has become known as a culture hawk in the federal cabinet. "It's the same decision."
The WTO panel ruled that Canada's attempts to protect its magazine industry by taxing Canadian editions of U.S. magazines -- so-called split-run editions -- violated world trade rules.
The dispute was triggered by a law that targeted Sports Illustrated, owned by Time Warner Inc., but was watched by publishers on both sides of the border.
The decision will be made available to other WTO members on March 14, after which Canada will have 60 days to appeal.

"In the next little while, they'll decide whether or nor there's anything in there that they wish to appeal," said Charles Larabie, spokesman for the Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.

Bax noted that Copps said after the interim ruling that Canada would appeal. While the decision was ultimately up to International Trade Minister Art Eggleton, Bax said it was unlikely the decision to appeal would change.
Various strategies were meanwhile being explored about to how to protect Canadian magazines while adhering to international trade obligations, she said.
